items.description: Pastes the internal clipboard into a target range with paste-special semantics: selectable content (values / formulas / formats / all / all-except-borders), an optional arithmetic operation against the existing target values, skip-blanks, and transpose. Relative formula references are shifted by the paste offset (except when transposing, where formulas are flattened to their computed value to avoid producing wrong references). Undo restores the overwritten cells exactly.

members.name: AffectedCellRefs
members.description: The cell references changed by the latest paste (for renderer invalidation).

items.description: Removes duplicate rows from a range, keeping the first occurrence of each distinct key-column combination and compacting the surviving rows upward within the range. Only the columns inside the range are touched (Excel/OnlyOffice semantics); cells outside the range stay put. The whole operation is a single atomic step: Undo restores the original layout exactly. Ranges that intersect a merged cell are rejected.

members.name: AffectedCellRefs
members.description: The cell references touched by the last Execute (for renderer invalidation).

members.name: HasMergeConflict

Replaces matched text within a single cell and supports undo. The cell's searchable text (displayed value or formula, per SearchIn) is rewritten and re-parsed through SpreadsheetValueParser. In Values mode formula cells are skipped so their formulas are never destroyed.

Turns the auto-filter on over a range (or moves it to a new range). Enabling the filter adds the header buttons but hides nothing until column criteria are set. Undo restores the previous filter and the previous row visibility.
Applies a style mutation to multiple cells and supports undo.

Sets the value and/or formula of a single cell and supports undo. Optionally applies a typed data type and an implied number format (the latter only when the cell still uses the General format), as produced by SpreadsheetValueParser.
Adds or replaces a data validation rule on a sheet range. Fully undoable: removes any previous rule that overlapped the same range and restores it on undo.
Sets a structured hyperlink on a cell. If the cell is empty and a display text is provided, the display text is written into the cell value. Supports undo.

Sorts a range by reordering whole rows (or columns when ByRows is set). Cell values, formulas and styles move with their row; relative formula references are shifted by the row delta of the move so they keep pointing at the same logical data. Undo restores the original cell layout exactly. Ranges that intersect merged cells are rejected.

items.description: An Excel-like spreadsheet component for viewing and editing tabular data. Since the ribbon v2 redesign it renders (in Full mode) an optional document header, the tabbed ribbon with named command groups, the formula bar with the fx mark and the commit/revert buttons, the canvas grid, the sheet tabs and the status bar. Supports cell editing, formulas, styling, multi-sheet workbooks and XLSX import/export.

examples.title: Basic spreadsheet
examples.code:
<TmSpreadsheet Height="500px"
               RowsCount="100"
               ColumnsCount="20"
               OnChange="HandleChange" />

@code {
    private void HandleChange(SpreadsheetChangeEventArgs args)
        => Console.WriteLine($"{args.CellRef} = {args.NewValue}");
}

examples.title: Load and export an XLSX workbook
examples.code:
<TmSpreadsheet @ref="_sheet" Data="@_xlsxBytes" />

<TmButton OnClick="DownloadAsync">Download</TmButton>

@code {
    private TmSpreadsheet? _sheet;
    private byte[]? _xlsxBytes;

    private async Task DownloadAsync()
    {
        var bytes = await _sheet!.ExportToExcelAsync();
        // hand the bytes to your download helper
    }
}

examples.title: Read-only view and programmatic edits
examples.code:
<TmSpreadsheet @ref="_sheet" Mode="SpreadsheetMode.Full" />

@code {
    private TmSpreadsheet? _sheet;

    protected override void OnAfterRender(bool firstRender)
    {
        if (!firstRender) return;
        _sheet!.SetCellValue("A1", "Total");
        _sheet.SetCellValue("B1", "=SUM(B2:B10)");
    }
}

items.description: The spreadsheet's context menu surface. It must be rendered as a SIBLING of the layout container: the container is container-type: inline-size (implied contain: layout), which makes it the containing block of a position:fixed menu, and a menu inside the scrolling grid would be clipped. On the mobile layout it is the core TmDrawer bottom sheet (modal: backdrop + focus trap, Escape closes it, 44px menuitem rows in the sans face); on desktop/tablet the anchored menu at the gesture's client point.

items.description: Find & replace panel for the spreadsheet. Owns the query/replacement text and search options locally and bubbles changes to the host, which performs the actual search/replace and reports the current match position back via MatchIndex / MatchCount.

parameters.description: The layout the panel renders. Auto reads the app-level viewport scope — never the panel's own container, which is position-absolute on the desktop layout, so measuring it would flip the mode on every render — and keeps the floating panel when the host provides no scope. Mobile renders the non-modal bottom sheet, Desktop and Tablet the floating panel; a forced value never imports an observer script.

items.description: The Format Cells dialog on the core TmModal frame: five tabs (Number, Alignment, Font, Border, Fill). On the Number tab the category is a keyboard-operable listbox on desktop/tablet and a core TmSelect above the options on a phone; decimal places use the core TmNumberInput stepper and the live preview is aligned like the format (numeric right, text left). The Border tab paints the package's registered tm-ss-border-* SVG icons, never Unicode box glyphs. Ctrl+Enter applies.

items.description: Dialog for inserting or editing a structured hyperlink on a cell. Supports four link kinds: Web, Email, InternalRef and NamedRange (named ranges come from the workbook). The dialog rides the core TmModal frame: the initial focus is the target field ("hl-target"), Escape dismisses through the frame's document-level listener and the focus returns to the grid (RestoreFocusTargetId). Ctrl+Enter saves from any form field; the footer buttons are the frame's own and never double-activate. The target field switches its inputmode with the kind (url / email). The form-field ids (#hl-type, #hl-target, #hl-subject, #hl-display, #hl-tooltip) are a published E2E contract and one dialog is open at a time.

items.description: The Insert Image dialog: one URL field plus a Cancel / Apply footer. It used to be inline markup inside TmSpreadsheet; it now rides the core TmModal frame, which owns the overlay, the dialog role, the initial focus on the URL field, the document-level Escape, the focus restore (to the grid) and the mobile sheet. The URL is validated with Uri.TryCreate and only an absolute http(s) address or a data: URI can be applied — Apply stays disabled and the field carries aria-invalid plus an inline alert until then. Enter applies from the field; applying raises the URL, which the spreadsheet writes to the active cell's ImageUrl (the canvas paints it).

items.description: Dialog for creating or editing a named range. Validates name syntax and the required fields, with an inline error per field (aria-invalid + role="alert") and the first invalid field taking the focus after a failed save. The dialog rides the core TmModal frame: the initial focus is the name field ("nr-name"), Escape dismisses through the frame's document-level listener and the focus returns to the grid (RestoreFocusTargetId) or to the Name Manager it was opened from, so a stacked dialog never strands the keyboard. Ctrl+Enter saves from any form field; the footer buttons are the frame's own and never double-activate. The form-field ids (#nr-name, #nr-refers, #nr-scope, #nr-sheet, #nr-comment) are a published E2E contract and one dialog is open at a time.

items.description: Name Manager dialog that lists all named ranges in the workbook, allows filtering, and raises events for New / Edit / Delete. The list is a WAI-ARIA grid with a roving tabindex: the selected row is the single tab stop and carries the DOM focus, Up/Down/Home/End move the selection, Enter edits the selected range, Delete deletes it (the neighbour takes the selection) and a double click edits. The dialog itself is a modal overlay whose role, aria-modal, accessible name, initial focus, Escape handling and focus restore come from the core TmFocusScope; all element ids are per instance and none is a selector contract.

items.description: Ribbon-style toolbar for the spreadsheet: one tab strip (Home, Insert, Data, View and the legacy File tab) followed by a row of named groups. Every group carries a stable, additive-only data-tm-group id (clipboard | font | alignment | number | cells | insert | links | data | view | file | custom), every tab and tabpanel carries data-tm-tab, custom groups also carry data-tool-id, and the tab strip follows the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern (per-instance ids, aria-controls/aria-labelledby, roving tabindex, ArrowLeft/Right/Home/End). Commands are large (icon above the label) or small (icon and label on one line); every icon is a TmIcon, and the cell-border, vertical-alignment and decimal marks are the package's own registered SVG icons. The border picker, the colour pickers and the Delete split render through the core TmOverlayPanel (browser top layer), so the ribbon row's horizontal overflow can never clip them. Contract: docs/spreadsheet.md.

items.description: The severity-driven validation alert on the core TmModal frame (alertdialog, aria-describedby, focus trap, Escape, focus restore). A Medium card places a large filled severity badge to the LEFT of the message and has no divider under the title. Stop offers only the acknowledge action (a backdrop click does nothing); Warning adds the keep-the-value action; Information keeps both. A rule's own ErrorAlert title/message wins over the severity defaults.

parameters.name: CancelText
parameters.description: Label of the cancel action. Null falls back to the localized "Cancel".

parameters.name: LayoutMode
parameters.description: The layout the alert renders. Auto follows the viewport scope (a sheet on the narrow one); a forced value pins the mode without measuring, so a test can render the mobile sheet without a DOM.

parameters.name: Message
parameters.description: The alert body text (the rule's own message). Null falls back to the severity's localized default.

parameters.name: OnCancel
parameters.description: Raised when the user cancels the alert (a backdrop click or the cancel action).

parameters.name: OnPrimary
parameters.description: Raised when the user accepts the alert (the only close path of a Stop alert).

parameters.name: PrimaryText
parameters.description: Label of the primary action. Null falls back to the severity's localized default ("Got it" for Stop, "Use anyway" for Warning/Information).

parameters.name: RestoreFocus
parameters.description: Whether closing the alert restores the focus it took. Defaults to true.

parameters.name: RestoreFocusTargetId
parameters.description: The id of the element focus returns to when the alert closes — the host spreadsheet passes its grid root, so focus lands on the grid rather than the toolbar button that opened the alert. Null falls back to the element focused before the alert opened.

parameters.name: Severity
parameters.description: How severe the message is. Stop blocks the value (a single acknowledge action, a backdrop click does nothing); Warning and Information ask whether the value should be kept. Defaults to Stop.

parameters.name: ShowCancel
parameters.description: Whether a cancel action exists. Null falls back to the severity: a Stop alert has none (it is a hard block), a Warning or Information confirm always offers one.

parameters.name: Title
parameters.description: The alert title (the rule's own title). Null falls back to the severity's localized default ("Invalid value" / "Value outside the recommended range" / "Note").
